blogs.title: Structured Finance Outlook for 2025: What Mid-Market Borrowers Should Watch
blogs.excerpt: Rate cuts, tighter bank appetite, and more bespoke structures are reshaping how growth companies access capital. Here is what finance teams should plan for this year.

author.name: Priya Sharma
author.about: Director, Debt Advisory. Priya advises mid-market companies on refinancing, acquisition finance, and capital structure reviews.

seo.title: Structured Finance Outlook 2025
seo.description: A practical view of structured finance trends for mid-market borrowers in 2025.
seo.primaryTopic: Structured Finance, Debt Advisory, and Mid-Market Capital Markets
seo.summary: Mid-market borrowers face a barbell market in 2025: plain working-capital lines remain accessible, but complex structures need stronger cash-flow proof and earlier lender outreach.
seo.targetQuery: What should mid-market borrowers expect from structured finance in 2025?
keyTakeaways: Lenders are prioritising cash-flow visibility over growth narratives alone.
Covenant-lite structures are harder to secure without scale or sponsor backing.
Documentation timelines are lengthening—start lender conversations earlier.
Club deals and syndication are increasingly common for mid-market ticket sizes.

faqs.question: Who is this outlook most relevant for?
faqs.answer: CFOs and founders at companies with ₹50–500 crore revenue evaluating debt or hybrid capital.

faqs.question: Are structured facilities still available for first-time borrowers?
faqs.answer: Yes, but expect tighter covenants, shorter initial tenors, and more detailed monthly reporting packs than in 2021–2022.

faqs.question: How early should we start a refinancing or new mandate?
faqs.answer: For maturities inside 18 months, begin lender dialogue at least six months ahead. Complex structures may need longer.

faqs.question: What data do lenders scrutinise most in 2025?
faqs.answer: Recurring revenue quality, customer concentration, working-capital seasonality, and credible forward cash forecasts with downside cases.

content.text: This nested paragraph survives even though the parent embed type is unsupported.
Borrowers entered 2025 with more clarity on rates, but less clarity on which lenders will compete for their mandate. The result is a
barbell market
: plain-vanilla working-capital lines remain accessible, while complex structured solutions require stronger preparation.
This article walks through what we are seeing on live mandates—use it as a reference when you pressure-test your own financing plan.
Three themes shaping mandates
Shorter tenors with extension options instead of long-dated bullet structures.
Greater emphasis on recurring revenue quality and customer concentration.
More club deals as individual banks manage sector exposure limits.
What “good” looks like in a lender pack
Three-year historical financials with
clear
normalisation schedules for non-recurring items.
Monthly cash-flow bridge for the last 12 months plus a 12-month forward view.
Facility use-of-proceeds tied to measurable milestones—not generic “growth capital”.
The best-prepared borrowers treat lender updates as an ongoing rhythm, not a one-off data dump at signing.
For a deeper checklist, see the
borrower readiness guide
on our resources hub.

seo.title: Refinancing Playbook for Founder-Led Businesses
seo.description: How to prepare for a refinancing process without disrupting day-to-day operations.
seo.summary: Begin refinancing prep six months out, clean the numbers before lender outreach, and compare full term sheets—not just headline rates.
keyTakeaways: Start refinancing work six months before maturity—not six weeks.
Normalise EBITDA and cash flow before sharing teasers with lenders.
Run a structured term-sheet comparison; headline rate is rarely the full story.

faqs.question: Can we talk to lenders before our maturity date?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most lenders expect exploratory conversations 9–12 months ahead for mid-market facilities. Early dialogue improves optionality.

faqs.question: What slows refinancing processes down most?
faqs.answer: Incomplete data rooms and unclear use-of-proceeds. Fixing those before outreach typically shortens timelines by several weeks.

faqs.question: Should founders join lender meetings?
faqs.answer: For founder-led businesses, yes—a credible growth narrative from leadership often matters as much as the numbers.

content.text: Founder-led businesses often delay refinancing work until a maturity date is within sight. That compresses negotiating leverage. A better approach is to treat refinancing as a
six-month project
with defined milestones.
Suggested timeline
T-6 months: validate historical cash flows and normalise one-off items.
T-4 months: shortlist lenders and share a concise teaser.
T-2 months: run a structured data room and term-sheet review.
Documents to prepare early
Audited accounts and management accounts (last 3 years).
Debt schedule with covenants, amortisation, and security summary.
Cap table and shareholder agreements if private equity is involved.
Lenders reward clarity. A concise teaser with honest risk flags beats a polished deck that omits known issues.

blogs.title: Valuation Updates That Actually Help Close Transactions
blogs.excerpt: Boards often commission valuations that satisfy compliance but do not help negotiators. The difference is in assumptions, comparables, and how findings are presented to counterparties.

author.name: Elena Vasquez
author.about: Head of Valuations. Elena leads fairness opinions and purchase-price allocation work for cross-border deals.

seo.title: Valuation Updates for Transactions
seo.description: Practical guidance on valuations that support negotiation—not just documentation.
keyTakeaways: Align valuation purpose with the audience—board, lender, or counterparty.
Sensitivity tables matter more than a single point estimate.
Update trading comps closer to signing, not only at mandate start.

faqs.question: When do we need a fairness opinion?
faqs.answer: Typically for related-party transactions, certain board fiduciary processes, or when lenders require independent support for collateral values.

faqs.question: How often should comps be refreshed?
faqs.answer: For active deals, refresh trading and transaction comps within 30 days of signing—or sooner if markets move sharply.

content.text: A transaction-ready valuation explains
why
a range is reasonable, not only what the range is. That distinction changes how investors and sellers engage with your numbers.
Common valuation methods
Discounted cash flow with explicit scenario and sensitivity tables.
Trading comparables adjusted for growth, margin, and liquidity differences.
Precedent transactions where deal terms are genuinely comparable.
Present all three where possible—even if one method is weighted more heavily in the final conclusion.
